thread.title: This overlooked stock in an increasingly hot sector is ready to bust out

author: Barbara Kollmeyer
title: This overlooked stock in an increasingly hot sector is ready to bust out
text:
Expect some big-name tech stocks to re-hog the limelight today.
Like Facebook, which is on a tear in premarket after dazzling investors with bulletproof earnings , such as a 49% revenue pop. Helping complete that FAANG earnings picture, Amazon and Microsoft are due after the close, with Apple finishing things off next Tuesday. (See buzz for more on Apple below).
With the vast number of results from major companies rolling out, it’s easy to overlook the outperformers that grab fewer headlines. That brings us to our call of the day , from Josh Beck and Alex Markgraff of KeyBanc Capital Markets, who say payments processing company PayPal PYPL, +2.74% is not getting enough credit for doing all the right things, right now.
“The perceived eBay risk is hyped, in our view. PayPal is moving beyond the ‘investment’ phase of consumer choice, and Venmo to the harvesting phase,” say Josh Beck and Alex Markgraff of KeyBanc Capital Markets, who recommend an overweight position on PayPal and a price target of $90 a share.
PayPal is up a mere 0.5% year to date, and sits at around $74.
MarketWatch The eBay concerns have to do with PayPal totally cutting the ties with the mothership over next five years and what that would do to its revenue. Some say eBay should represent a smaller and smaller chunk for the payments processing company, and the KeyBanc analysts agree.
The analysts say shares reflect a 100% discount for those eBay risks, yet their own estimates point to a 9% risk to operating profits in the next 5 years from a full break from the online auctioneer.
But Beck and Markgraff argue that PayPal gets no credit for “upside opportunities,” such as mobile-payment app Venmo or partnerships with JP Morgan JPM, +0.10% , Barclays BARC, -1.41% , Grubhub GRUB, +3.10% , Samsung and others.
Investors are also forgetting that PayPal has real potential to increase its market share. Share buybacks and M&A action for the company are also possible.
Steve Alexander, editor at MagicDilligence, recently referred to payments processing as a “golden bucket” industry .
Firstly, it’s predictable, with tons of recurring revenue, which is also stable. Plus, the sector is growing as even governments move to electronic payments. And once a business picks a payment processor such as PayPal or Square SQ, +4.45% , they’re likely to stick with it for the long run.
Key market gauges The Dow DJIA, +0.99% , S&P 500 SPX, +1.04% and Nasdaq COMP, +1.64% are all off to a pretty upbeat start.

European markets SXXP, +0.94% are up a bit , while Hong Kong HSI, -1.06% and China SHCOMP, -1.38% shares kept falling .
The yield on the 10-year government bond TMUBMUSD10Y, -0.03% is hovering at 3%.
Gold GCM8, -0.01% is ticking up as the dollar DXY, +0.01% has cooled off some. Oil CLM8, -0.18% is rising .
See the Market Snapshot column for more.
The chart Facebook is up more than 6% in premarket, which means a pretty big day may be ahead for investors in those shares.
MarketWatch Rising before the bell If those gains hold, the social media giant could be looking at its best one-day rise since April 28, 2016 , when shares surged 7% after some equally dazzling first-quarter results and a 52% bump in revenue.
Earnings Bloomberg News/Landovs Reporting early, GM GM, +0.37% shares are down after it posted a 60% profit drop, but still beat forecasts. Southwest LUV, -0.98% , UPS UPS, +4.25% are among the many names that reported ahead of the open.
After the bell, Amazon AMZN, +3.96% , Microsoft MSFT, +2.11% , Intel INTC, +3.25% and Starbucks SBUX, +2.89% will be in the spotlight.
Earnings previews: Intel | Microsoft | Amazon
Outside of Facebook, late Wednesday earnings are boosting Ford F, +2.88% shares. The auto maker said it will stop putting money into sedans in North America. AMD AMD, +13.70% is another big post-results gainer, along with Chipotle CMG, +24.44% EBay EBAY, -5.59% is faring less well after its report.
The buzz Samsung 005930, +2.69% shot up 3% overnight after posting its fourth-straight record quarter . But as some point out, the tech group revealed weakness in its display panel segment — and Samsung is an Apple AAPL, +0.35% supplier, chiefly of OLED panels for the iPhone X, notes a report on iAppleInsider . That could be a “harbinger of slower than expected iPhone X sales,” says the report. We’ll see next week.
Read: Can Facebook, Apple and Google keep powering tech’s growth?
The ECB kept rates unchanged and made no changes to its statement. At a press conference, ECB President Mario Draghi has been playing down soft economic data.
Not a fan. Cubeyou’s CEO says Facebook threw it under the bus with regards to the fallout over collecting data from users.
Trump told “Fox & Friends” this morning that he won’t stay away from the Justice Department, citing the “witch hunt” over the possible collusion between his campaign and Russia.
Weekly jobless claims dropped 9,000, clinging to a 45-year low . Durable goods orders surged on Boeing orders , advance trade in goods and housing vacancies are among the economic data on tap today.
The stat The 17th million bitcoin is likely to be mined Thursday, according to Blockchain info cited by CoinDesk . That will mark the first million-bitcoin milestone to be reached since mid-2016, and brings the cryptocurrency that much closer to the absolute limit of 21 million.
Bitcoin BTCUSD, +1.50% has slipped back under $9,000 .

The Quote: Getty Images “It is extremely regrettable.We have asked that the dessert not be served.” — a spokeswoman for the Japanese Foreign Ministry, commenting on a mango mousse on Seoul’s menu for Friday’s summit between North and South Korea.
The “distasteful” mousse will be in the shape of small islands whose ownership is disputed by Japan and South Korea, whose citizens still harbor resentment over Japan’s colonization of the country.
Meanwhile, anticipation is building for the Koreas summit, which kicks off when Kim Jong Un steps into the demilitarized zone on Friday morning.
